ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle B=90^\circ$, $\angle C=30^\circ$, $DE$ is perpendicular to and bisects $AC$, intersecting $BC$ at point $E$, with $CE=2$, then how much is $BC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since DE is the perpendicular bisector of AC, and CE=2,\\
it follows that AE=CE,\\
which means $\angle C=\angle$EAC$=30^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle$BAE$=30^\circ$,\\
hence $EB=\frac{1}{2}EA=1$,\\
thus BC=BE+EC$=\boxed{3}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, B is at the upper left; BC is the hypotenuse from B down to the right to C, point E is located on BC; from E downward draw line segment ED intersecting AC at D, in the figure ED is perpendicular to AC; line segment AE is also drawn, located inside the triangle. Reasoning: From the meaning of the problem, DE is perpendicular to and bisects AC, so DE is the perpendicular bisector of AC. Point E is on this perpendicular bisector, therefore EA=EC. It is known that CE=2, so AE=2. Because E is on BC, ∠ACE equals ∠C in triangle ABC, namely 30°. In triangle AEC, EA=EC, so the base angles are equal, ∠EAC=∠ACE=30°. Also because ∠B=90° and ∠C=30°, ∠BAC=60°. Therefore ∠BAE=∠BAC-∠EAC=60°-30°=30°. In right triangle ABE, AE is the hypotenuse, and ∠BAE=30°, so the side BE opposite the 30° angle equals half of the hypotenuse AE, namely BE=1. E is on BC and CE=2, so BC=BE+CE=1+2=3.
